title: Jensen Huang on OpenAI, extreme co-design and why accelerated computing wins (BG2, 2025)
summary: Jensen explains the OpenAI partnership, the three scaling laws, and why general-purpose computing is giving way to accelerated computing and AI. He covers extreme co-design as Nvidia's moat, how to build a market as a startup, sovereign AI, China, immigration, and why AI augments jobs.

principles.text: Optimize model, algorithm, system and chip together. When the chip stops getting faster, innovate outside the box.
principles.quote: Extreme code design means that you have to optimize the model, algorithm, system, and chip at the same time.

principles.text: Create a startup before the market grows. Take 100% of a tiny market, and hope it gets big.
principles.quote: You're supposed to take 100% of a tiny company, a tiny industry, which is what Nvidia did did, right?

principles.text: The 'take a few percent of a huge market' idea is a fallacy.
principles.quote: You're not supposed to come up as a startup when the market's a trillion dollars large.

principles.text: Nvidia sees itself as an AI infrastructure company, not a chip company. It sells in whatever way customers prefer to buy.
principles.quote: NVIDIA is really an AI infrastructure company. You know, we are your AI infrastructure partner

principles.text: When Moore's law stalls, the cost of tokens only falls if performance rises every year. That is why Nvidia moved to an annual cadence.
principles.quote: we have to increase our per performance annually at a pace that keeps up with that exponential.

principles.text: Facing a fast exponential, get on early and figure out the rest on the way. Don't try to predict where it will be.
principles.quote: If you have a train that's about to get faster and faster and go exponential, the only thing that you really need to do is get on it.
